answer: Distinct Habitat Attestation. Each identity must present a fresh physical sample (water, soil) from a unique GPS cell, verified by scattered sensors that also record a local acoustic fingerprint. A lotus pond cell and a sable burrow cell yield different readings, so one operator cannot mass-produce valid samples from one room. Every new identity costs a separate field trip plus sample collection; collusion across sites imposes travel and hardware overhead that scales linearly with fake identities. Each attestation carries an echo signature tied to its cell.
